:star: Hi everyone, Concordia AI is currently recruiting for <https://concordia-ai.com/career/ai-safety-researcher/|researchers> and <https://concordia-ai.com/career/ai-safety-research-engineer/|research engineers> to join their frontier AI safety evaluations team. Concordia AI is an AI safety organization based in Beijing and Singapore. Though I no longer work at Concordia, I think that this position has the potential to be extremely impactful due to Concordia’s strong relationship with leading Chinese AI developers.

The positions would require relocating to either Singapore or Beijing. Mandarin Chinese capability is extremely helpful, but they would also consider exceptional candidates without Chinese language skills.

If you are interested in applying, please DM me or email me (<mailto:jason@astralisfoundation.org|jason@astralisfoundation.org>), since the official deadline has already passed.

Trajectory Labs is looking to hire researchers, initially on a contract basis ($100-150/hr) to help us to teach AI to do conceptual x-risk reduction research, especially in AI governance, macrostrategy, econ theory, alignment theory, and conceptual AI safety (like the redwood blog). You will talk to top experts in your field, read their papers, and distill the insights into evals that measure whether LLMs are improving at these tasks. Your research taste gets distilled directly into the frontier models. You can work with me, Oscar Gilg, Stefan Schubert, Joar Skalse, Gustav Alexandrie, Aron Vallinder, and others. Feel free to apply <https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/trajectory-labs/8df41cd8-c9da-4d9b-a750-f91522aa4f83|here> and you can also contact me e.g. on this slack if you do apply.

Applications are open for roles in the California Attorney General’s Office that will support the enforcement of consumer protection and technology laws, *including SB 53, California’s frontier AI safety legislation*:

	*<https://calcareers.ca.gov/CalHrPublic/Jobs/JobPosting.aspx?JobControlId=535414|Consumer Protection Attorney (Deputy Attorney General)>*
As a Deputy Attorney General in the Consumer Protection Section of the California Department of Justice, the person in this role will “handle cutting-edge investigations and enforcement actions under California’s consumer protection and privacy laws.” In addition, attorneys will “draft amicus briefs on significant consumer protection issues, review proposed legislation and regulations affecting consumers, and engage in consumer education and advocacy.” AI is a potential area of focus and familiarity with machine learning is a desired qualification. “Applicants should have experience with complex litigation, possess exceptional writing and research skills, be persuasive oral advocates and negotiators, and exercise sound judgment.”
*Location:* Must live in California, with hybrid work out of an office in Los Angeles, Oakland, San Francisco, or San Diego.
	*Salary:* $95,628–$202,596 (dependent on the classification hired at)
	*Position type:* Full-time, permanent
	*Application Deadline:* Until filled


The Attorney General’s Office is responsible for enforcing SB 53 by bringing actions against large frontier developers that fail to publish or follow a compliant safety framework, fail to report critical safety incidents, or that “make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models.”

California’s Attorney General is one of only a few entities with the authority to enforce frontier AI safety and transparency requirements, and California is well positioned to pass much stronger AI legislation in 2027. If that legislation passes, it could make this office among the world’s most important enforcement authorities for frontier AI safety.

Please email <mailto:implementation@secureaiproject.org|implementation@secureaiproject.org> if you’re interested in applying to the role. *If you are thinking of applying, we strongly recommend that you <https://calendly.com/skye-secureaiproject/meeting-on-implementation-roles|schedule a call> with us before you apply. The application process can be confusing, and it’s easy to accidentally get autorejected by an automated application system.* Note: Secure AI Project is not affiliated with this job.

<https://princint.ai/|Principles of Intelligence (PrincInt)> is hiring Research Scientists to work on Ambitious Mechanistic Interpretability (AMI).

:date: <https://airtable.com/appBFp087UqOuMFld/pag1xYu2HOdHZY0W6/form|Applications> close on November 20

Full-time, fully remote role to lead research projects at the intersection of physics and mechanistic interpretability. See below for more details:

• *Work*: Develop tractable data models inspired by statistical physics, quantify the relationship between data structure and learned features, and build synthetic datasets to benchmark and improve interpretability tools. The team is currently focused on exploring a data model based on high-dimensional percolation theory.
• *Team*: A small team conducting interdisciplinary research on synthetic data models. You’ll help shape the team’s research direction, own projects end to end, and mentor junior researchers and fellows.
• *Terms*: Full-time; we’re open to either full employment or a contractor arrangement, depending on location and candidate preference. Fully remote, with a strong preference for candidates based in or able to spend significant time in London (UK) and/or the Bay Area (US).
    ◦ *Start date:* January 2027.
• *Salary*: $125,000–$170,000 USD gross per year, set by seniority and location.
• *Profile*: PhD or equivalent research experience in a technical field such as math, physics, machine learning, neuroscience, computer science, or complexity science; working knowledge of neural networks and deep learning, including hands-on model training; experience with scientific computing in Python; strong motivation to contribute to AI safety.
• *Process*: Application form, screening call, remote interview, research talk, paid one-day remote work trial, references. Rolling review.
:link: *Find the complete job description here:* <https://princint.ai/research-scientists-at-principles-of-intelligence/|princint.ai/research-scientists-at-principles-of-intelligence>
